newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower on long liquidation.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed lower on Monday, on long liquidation by local investors, but market players were reluctant to trade actively ahead of the USDA crop reports to announced later today, traders said.
Prices ranged from 50 to 150 yen lower, with the benchmark July 1998 contract down 110 yen at 13,310 yen per tonne.

Light long liquidation by individual investors capped the topside throughout the day, traders said. A decline in prices on the CBOT Project A overnight trading accelerated selling in the afternoon sessions, they said.
"We'd like to see how USDA crop reports will affect the market," a brokerage house trader said.
Open interest in Tokyo corn futures fell to 413,768 lots as of June 27 from 423,663 as of June 2.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.45 per bushel at 0715 GMT, down from $2.46-1/4 at Friday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $7.91-1/2 a bushel at 0715 GMT, against $7.87 at Friday's close.
